About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About The Role

Companies are adopting AI across more teams, but most still struggle to produce real workflows, measurable outcomes, and efficient spend. Ramp’s AI Solutions team helps customers turn that spend into working systems: agents, automations, and integrations that run real finance operations, built on top of Ramp’s growing AI product stack, including Glass, Inspect, Router, and Token Spend Management.

As a software engineer on AI Solutions, you'll co-lead customer engagements with an AI Solutions Strategist
while also helping turn repeated customer needs into platform capabilities across Ramp’s AI product stack. The Strategist
owns business discovery, the ROI story, stakeholder alignment, and rollout planning. You
own the technical side: discovery, solution design, prototyping, implementation, production readiness, and the product feedback loop back into our platform and AI primitives.

This is a deeply client-facing, hands-on building role based in New York, with occasional travel depending on engagements. You'll take projects from a customer's first workflow-discovery sessions through launch and into steady, measurable production use — then turn what you learned into reusable product patterns the next customer can adopt without starting from zero.

What You'll Do

Ship production AI workflows for the companies we partner with — agents, automations, and integrations their teams use every day.
Translate customer work into platform work by identifying needs across deployments and helping improve Ramp’s AI primitives.
Make the next deployment easier by turning customer specific work into reusable components, product feedback, reference architectures, and playbooks.
Run technical discovery with customers: current workflows, systems, data quality, constraints, and what's blocking adoption.
Turn customer goals into concrete requirements, including security, privacy, reliability, performance, scalability, and cost.
Prototype fast with end users to de-risk the approach before you build it out.
Own the technical plan end to end: architecture and data flow, integrations across Ramp and customer systems, permissions and auditability, evals and acceptance tests, and monitoring and runbooks.
Measure what you ship — quality, adoption, and cost — and stay with it until it's reliable, supportable, and handed off.

A track record of building from 0 to 1 in ambiguous environments: finding the real problem, shipping a first version quickly, learning from users, and hardening it over time.
Hands-on experience building LLM systems — agents, RAG, evals, and monitoring — and sound judgment on trade-offs like quality, latency, cost, and model choice.
Strong coding ability in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java, Go, or similar.
Comfort working across APIs, integrations, data pipelines, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure), and designing systems that are secure and scale.
Experience working directly with customers or end users: you can scope an ambiguous problem with a room of stakeholders and write clear technical docs afterward.

Background in forward deployed engineering, solutions architecture, technical consulting, or sales engineering.
Familiarity with finance operations workflows such as AP, procurement, expenses, close, reconciliation, and reporting.
Experience turning repeated customer needs into reusable product primitives, internal tools, or implementation playbooks.
Experience optimizing AI cost or performance, such as model routing, caching, or token spend analysis.

-This role is not advisory. The successful candidate will be expected to sit close to the business, understand front-office and operational workflows, write code, test solutions, debug issues, and help move AI use cases from concept to controlled production adoption.

Roles and Responsibilities

Evaluating AI models with benchmarks, calibrated model-based scoring, and human review to identify performance gaps and guide improvements

Creating visualizations and explaining model findings to clients, connecting technical results to business questions and practical recommendations

Reviewing junior team members’ analytical work and providing feedback on methods, documentation, and technical standards

You should not apply for this role if you will require Toyota to assist with immigration support or sponsorship now or in the future.

Who We're Looking For

Toyota Financial Services (TFS) Technology team is looking for a highly motivated person to fill a role as an ML/AI Security Lead within the Security Intelligence Engineering organization. You'll own the intelligence layer of a new AI-powered security platform — starting with prompt engineering and managed AI service integration, then progressing to fine-tuning models on enterprise security data, and building a multi-model serving and routing layer. This role is what makes the organization own its intelligence rather than renting it from a vendor. You'll train models that understand the specific security environment, build the feedback loops that make them better over time, and ensure the AI layer delivers high accuracy on alert triage while keeping costs predictable through intelligent model routing.

What You'll Be Doing

Design and implement prompt engineering patterns for managed AI service integration
Build training data pipelines from the security data lake — curating, labeling, and versioning datasets from real enterprise security telemetry
Fine-tune models on organization-specific security data — alert triage, risk scoring, finding classification
Implement the analyst feedback loop — capturing human corrections to continuously improve model accuracy
Build model evaluation frameworks with rigorous metrics (F1, precision, recall, false positive rates) benchmarked against analyst agreement
Design and implement a model routing layer — directing each task to the optimal model based on complexity, latency requirements, and cost
Monitor models in production for drift, accuracy degradation, and emerging failure modes
Implement centralized token usage monitoring for leadership visibility into AI consumption and cost control
Collaborate with the Lead Engineer on agent architectures — multi-agent orchestration, tool use, and autonomous triage workflows
Deploy and manage model inference endpoints across cloud ML services and container-based serving
Build the analyst feedback loop: approval/rejection signals in dashboards feeding back into retraining pipelines
What you bring
3+ years in applied ML/AI engineering (not research-only — production deployment required)
Hands-on experience with LLM fine-tuning — LoRA, QLoRA, or full fine-tuning on domain-specific data
Experience with cloud ML platforms (e.g., AWS SageMaker): training jobs, hyperparameter tuning, model registry, endpoint deployment
PyTorch proficiency for model training and custom architecture
Experience building evaluation pipelines — automated metrics, human evaluation protocols, A/B testing
Understanding of transformer architectures and attention mechanisms (not just API calls)
Python fluency with production engineering practices (testing, CI/CD, monitoring)
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain model behavior and limitations to non-ML stakeholders

Added bonus if you have

Experience with security or cybersecurity data — alert classification, threat detection, anomaly detection
Familiarity with model serving at scale (vLLM, Triton Inference Server, Tensor RT optimization)
Hugging Face Ecosystem Experience Model Hub, tokenizers, datasets library, PEFT
Experience with RAG architecture and vector databases
Background in multi-model routing or mixture-of-experts approaches
Understanding of agentic AI patterns — tool use, chain-of-thought, multi-step reasoning
Experience with model cost optimization — quantization, distillation, caching strategies
Self-motivated individual who thrives in ambiguous environments and can build processes from the ground up

Job Overview

Job Overview

Who We Are

Relativity is a leading legal data intelligence company building technology that helps users organize data, discover the truth, and act on it with confidence. Our AI-powered, cloud platform, RelativityOne, transforms massive volumes of complex information into actionable insights for litigation, investigations, regulatory inquiries, data breach responses, and other high-stakes legal work where accuracy and trust are crucial.

The world’s largest law firms, corporations, and government agencies rely on Relativity’s legal AI software to securely surface and manage the most relevant and impactful information in their matters. Beyond our commercial impact, we are committed to expanding access to technology and supporting pro bono legal work.

What We Do

claiR is Relativity's conversational AI experience, built for lawyers at the world's leading law firms. Running inside the Relativity aiR platform, claiR is an agentic surface into Relativity's petabytes of matter intelligence, letting users search, enrich, and generate work product from their data, with answers grounded in the matter's documents and backed by citations. The claiR team builds and ships this experience, from the AI and retrieval systems that reason across a matter to the web interface that lawyers and case teams use to explore their data and collaborate.

Job Description And Requirements

ABOUT THE ROLE

This role offers an opportunity to grow as a full-stack AI engineer on the team building claiR, the conversational AI experience lawyers use to ask questions, search, and draft from their matter data. You will work alongside the engineers and applied scientists who build claiR and gain direct exposure to how agentic features are designed, evaluated, and shipped. You will begin with well-defined features across the stack and grow toward end-to-end ownership of agentic features.

This Senior AI Engineer role is designed for a mid-to-high level engineer ready to grow quickly. The role reports to a Lead Engineer on claiR at Relativity and may be based remotely in the United States or in our Chicago office.

What You’ll Do

Build features across the full stack of claiR, including agent tools, prompt and context changes, services and API endpoints, and front-end work in the claiR web app.
Work with applied scientists to extend claiR’s agentic functionality with new capabilities and features.
Write and extend evaluations, run them, and learn to interpret the results. Ship changes behind feature flags and monitor production outcomes.
Learn and practice a modern software development lifecycle from day one through small, frequent commits, feature-flagged deployments, fast rollbacks, and best-in-class agentic engineering tools.
Fix bugs, improve reliability, and add tests while developing an understanding of how agentic systems fail.
Pair with Senior and Lead engineers on design and code reviews. Ask questions and document what you learn so others can benefit.
Take on increasingly ambiguous problems as you demonstrate readiness.

Required

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

5+ years of professional software development experience or equivalent demonstrated ability, such as a strong open-source track record, a shipped product, or substantial internship experience.
Working proficiency in Python and C#, plus hands-on experience building full-stack web applications with a front end such as React, services, and a relational database using SQL.
Hands-on experience building an agentic solution with LLMs, even at a small scale, such as an agent, a retrieval-augmented generation application, or a tool-using assistant. Ability to explain system prompts, tool calls, embeddings, and common failure points.
Basic familiarity with cloud services such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, containers, and CI/CD.
Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and writing clean, tested code.
Clear written and spoken English and a preference for simple solutions over clever ones.

WHY WE COULD BE A GREAT FIT

Impactful Mission

Build systems that help customers organize data, discover the truth, and act on it in high-stakes legal matters.

Engineering at Scale

Work on distributed, cloud-native systems that process large volumes of data.

Cutting-Edge Technology

Build with AI, cloud platforms, and scalable architectures shaping legal tech.

Growth and Ownership

Gain experience owning systems end-to-end across cloud and distributed environments.

Collaborative Culture

Work in a team focused on knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.

Inclusive Environment

Diverse perspectives create stronger teams and better outcomes.

Competitive salary, benefits, DTO, parental leave, and equity program.

Relativity is committed to competitive, fair, and equitable compensation practices.

This position is eligible for total compensation which includes a competitive base salary, an annual performance bonus, and long-term incentives.

Algorithms, Big Data, Cloud Computing, Computer Vision, Data Science, Deep Learning, Natural Language, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Project Management, Software Engineering

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
new_jobs.description:
About QuoteWell

We started as a vertical SaaS company in insurance and grew into running our own insurance brokerage, QuoteWell. That taught us what applying AI in insurance really takes: what works in production, what isn’t very useful, and what compounds into a lasting advantage.

We then spun that experience out into its own company. Third Plane is built to bring this operating model to retail insurance agencies outside QuoteWell, across the country. We’ve just closed fresh funding to scale it.

Our CEO, Joey Bouchard, built and ran applied AI teams at Palantir. We combine that technical rigor with years of hands-on insurance operations experience to help agencies deploy AI that works in the real world. (Why insurance is worth this attention.)

Our CEO, Joey Bouchard, built and ran applied AI teams at Palantir. We bring that technical rigor together with years of hands-on insurance operations experience to help agencies deploy AI that works in the real world. (Why insurance is worth this attention.)

Why this role exists

Brokerage execution runs on heroics. Service quality depends on who owns the account, how overloaded they are, and what they happen to remember at the right moment. A submission gets marketed broadly, or it doesn't. A renewal gets the same rigor as new business, or it doesn't. A missing detail gets chased, or it stalls.

We don't think that's inevitable. Brokerage execution can be made systematic: software, automation, and AI carrying disciplined follow-through alongside human experts, inside clear bounds, in a regulated environment.

The hard part isn't the model call. It's governability — making AI accountable enough to trust with real deal flow. Who is the AI acting for? What is it allowed to do? What happens when it's wrong? In a regulated industry, those aren't side questions. They're the engineering problem.

We've been answering them inside our own wholesale brokerage for years. That's where we test whether the model actually produces more reliable, scalable, and consistent service. If it doesn't work for us, it doesn't deserve to be packaged for the market. Now we're packaging it.

The role

Our Forward Deployed Engineers sit at the point where our platform, meets the messy reality of a customer's agency. You own the outcome at the customer. You also own the signal back to the rest of the company.

A typical month: you're embedded at a retail agency, working alongside their operators. You're identifying the workflows where heroics break down — submissions, renewals, follow-up, the work that today depends on someone's memory — and you're building governed AI execution into those workflows on Terminal. You're calibrating where humans stay (judgment, relationships, accountability) and where the system carries the standard (follow-through, coordination, attention).

The hardest and most interesting part: making it trustworthy. How AI decisions get reviewed, attributed, and defended. That work is what determines whether any of this can actually live in production.

Then you bring it all back. Engineering, Product, and Design need to know what generalizes and what doesn't, so the platform compounds across every customer instead of fragmenting into one-offs. You're the conduit.

What you'll do

Embed at a retail agency and own customer-side execution end to end
Build governed AI workflows on Terminal — integrating with AMS, carrier portals, email, and the systems an agency actually runs on
Identify which parts of an agency's operation can be made system-governed without losing the judgment that has to stay with people
Design the review, attribution, and override patterns that let a regulated business trust the system
Carry field signal back to Engineering, Product, and Design so the platform scales rather than splinters
Represent QuoteWell with customers — scope, troubleshoot, and reason about problems out loud, in their conference room
Travel to customer sites ~25% of the time

What we're looking for

1-5 years shipping production software (Python and/or TypeScript a plus)
Strong engineering foundation — CS degree typical, talented dropouts welcome
Hands-on experience with modern AI application patterns, or the aptitude and hunger to get there fast
Someone we can trust in front of a customer: troubleshoot, scope, and reason out loud, in the room
Genuine appetite to learn an industry deeply. Insurance is a financial supply chain puzzle, and we expect you to want to understand it
Genuine hustle. The kind of person who walks into Monday with a working prototype of something they spotted on Friday
Willingness to travel

What you get

A real production model to build on, not a slide deck.
Our wholesale brokerage is the proof point — you're scaling something that already works.
Direct mentorship from Joey,
who built and ran applied AI at Palantir before this.
A leadership trajectory.
Hire #1 or #2 on Recon, with a clear path to Applied AI Lead and beyond as we scale.
An industry that matters.
Insurance is one of the largest financial markets in the world and one of the least systematized.

These first few roles set the cultural tone for everything that comes after. If you want to understand what this role actually is, what it isn't, and what it likely means for your career — apply and reach out.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
new_jobs.description:
About Nevis

Nevis is building the world’s first AI wealth management platform. We are building the system financial advisors will run on for the next decade. Our AI completes work, automates workflows end to end, and frees advisors to spend more time with clients. In the future, every wealth management firm will run on Nevis.

Nevis was founded by an exceptional team of ex-Revolut executives and has raised $110 million in just two years
, including a $70 million Series B led by EQT Ventures & Growth
, backed by world-leading investors including Sequoia Capital, ICONIQ, and Ribbit.

The Role

We are looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to be the technical counterpart for our customers and make sure every implementation succeeds.

When one of the largest wealth management firms in the country decides to run on Nevis, you are the engineer in the room with them. You learn how their business actually works, translate that into what we build and configure, and own the technical side of the deployment from first workshop to a platform their advisors use every day. You work with their engineers, their operations team and their vendors, and you stay their technical point of contact long after go-live.

The work spans whatever the deployment needs: integrations with the systems they already run, getting their data into our platform, configuring and deploying AI agents and workflows against their real processes, prototyping fast to show what is possible, and being the person who diagnoses it when something does not behave the way anyone expected.

You will be trusted by the customer and relied on internally, so two things have to be true at once. You have to be precise, because these firms make decisions on the numbers we show them. And you have to move fast with whatever tools get you there, because the problems are novel and nobody is handing you a specification

What You’ll Do

Own the technical side of enterprise deployments end to end, from initial scoping through go-live and expansion
Be the customer's main technical point of contact, working alongside their engineers, operations teams and leadership
Understand how each firm operates deeply enough to translate their workflows into what Nevis builds, configures and automates for them
Design and deliver the integrations and data flows a deployment depends on, working with our engineering teams to make the pipes right
Configure and deploy AI agents and automated workflows against real customer processes, and tune them until they hold up in production
Build prototypes and demos fast, so customers can see what is possible before anyone commits to building it
Diagnose and resolve technical issues in live deployments, and be honest with customers about what the platform can and cannot do
Partner with Deployment Strategists on the commercial relationship, giving them the technical grounding that wins and grows accounts
Feed what you learn in the field back into the product, shaping the roadmap so every future customer inherits it

Who You Are

You have 3+ years in a forward deployed, solutions engineering, technical implementation or similar customer-facing engineering role at a high-growth technology company
You are a strong engineer. Python and SQL are second nature, and you are comfortable working across systems, APIs and messy real-world data
You have put LLMs and agentic tooling into production, and you have judgment about where they are reliable and where they are not
You build fast. You would rather ship something working and iterate than design something perfect on paper
You are precise about numbers. You know the difference between an honest "the data cannot answer that" and a confident wrong answer, and you know which one costs more
You communicate exceptionally well with people who are not engineers. You can walk a COO through what you built and where it is weak without losing them
You have low ego and high ownership. You do what needs to be done and the outcome matters more than the credit
You are comfortable with ambiguity, and you bring clarity to unstructured problems rather than frustration
You are happy to travel and work onsite with customers
STEM degree from a top university, or equivalent demonstrated experience

Nice to Have

Prior experience in wealth management, financial services or fintech
Familiarity with the US RIA landscape, including how large advisory firms are structured, regulated and operated
Experience with data integration, pipelines or systems migration at enterprise scale
You are at the frontier of using LLM-powered workflows in your day-to-day work, with hands-on fluency across tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or similar

Why Join Nevis?

Work alongside a high-calibre founding team backed by some of the best investors in the world
A fast-paced, high-growth environment with the opportunity to shape how the business operates
Be part of a mission-driven company transforming the wealth management industry with huge potential for global impact
15 days’ annual leave & Bank Holidays

Competitive salary and benefits package, including company equity

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Agentic Platform
new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

About North

North is Cohere's cutting-edge AI workspace platform, designed to revolutionize the way enterprises utilize AI. It offers a secure and customizable environment, allowing companies to deploy AI while maintaining control over sensitive data. North integrates seamlessly with existing workflows, providing a trusted platform that connects AI agents with workplace tools and applications.

Why this role?

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how enterprises harness the power of AI in real-world applications. As a bridge between our core North product and our clients’ engineering teams, you’ll be at the forefront of solving complex problems and securely integrating AI into critical sectors such as finance, healthcare, and telecommunications.

We’re looking for Software Engineers with Applied AI experience who can own the design, build, and deployment of agentic workflows powered by Large Language Models (LLMs), from early prototypes to production-grade AI agents, to deliver concrete business value in enterprise workflows. You’ll work closely with customers on real-world business problems, often building first-of-their-kind agent workflows that integrate LLMs with tools, APIs, and data sources. While our pace is startup-fast, the bar is enterprise-high: agents must be reliable, observable, safe, and auditable from day one.

Note: between 20 - 40% travel anticipated.

In This Role, You Will

Work closely with our enterprise customers to translate high-value, ambiguous business problems into well-framed agentic workflows with clear success criteria and evaluation methodologies
Lead the design, build, and delivery of LLM-powered agents that reason, plan, and act across tools, APIs, and sensitive enterprise data sources, with enterprise-grade reliability and performance
Build and ship features for North, our AI workspace platform, working across the full product lifecycle from conceptualization through production
Take ownership of scoping and shaping use cases end-to-end, flexing into whatever technical area the problem demands (including frontend) to drive the most effective solution
Contribute to shared frameworks and patterns that enable consistent, high-quality delivery across customers and teams
Drive clarity in ambiguous situations, build alignment, and raise engineering quality across the organization
Travel up to 20–40% to work on-site with customers and partners

You May Be a Good Fit If

You have hands-on experience building and deploying production-grade software in Python; you write clean, testable, observable, scalable code
You've built and deployed highly performant RAG and agentic applications, including agents that plan and execute multi-step tasks using patterns like ReAct or Plan-and-Execute
You're deeply familiar with the LLM stack: frontier models, vector databases, and orchestration frameworks
You have a proven ability to build robust evaluation frameworks, moving well beyond trial and error, to measure agent accuracy, safety, and latency
You’re experienced working directly with customers and can lead technical discussions with enterprise stakeholders, translating ambiguous business needs into concrete technical specs
You have experience owning the full scope of a use case end-to-end
You thrive in fast-paced and ambiguous environments and can execute well even when priorities are shifting

It's a Bonus If You Have

Experience setting architectural standards for AI and agentic systems across distributed teams
Experience flexing into unfamiliar technical areas, such as frontend, when the problem calls for it
Exposure to regulated or sensitive industry environments (finance, healthcare, telecoms)
Experience with enterprise security, compliance, or auditability requirements for AI systems

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

new_jobs.description:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About The Role

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at Commure, you'll play a crucial role in collaborating directly with healthcare clients, understanding their needs, and actively participating in the design and implementation of customized solutions. This immersive experience offers you the chance to be at the heart of healthcare technology, contributing to projects that enhance patient access, affordability, and care quality.

In this highly visible position, you'll provide essential technical support, tackle various challenges, and maintain vital documentation. Additionally, by keeping pace with evolving healthcare technology trends, you'll contribute innovative ideas and solutions. Your contributions will be instrumental in advancing our mission to revolutionize healthcare through technology.

What You’ll Do

Be willing to travel up to 20% of the time to client site, build on site, and demo.
Participate in the implementation process, aiding in the integration of our solutions into client settings.
Provide technical assistance and contribute to problem-solving during deployment and integration phases.
Work collaboratively with healthcare clients to understand their technology needs, compliance requirements, and patient care goals.
Support our development and engineering teams in crafting tailored solutions for the healthcare industry.
Help identify and address technical challenges encountered during project implementation.
Assist in creating and updating technical documentation to streamline client onboarding and system maintenance.
Keep informed about the latest trends in healthcare technology and regulations to help propose relevant solutions.
Visit new places and meet interesting people in the heart of healthcare

What You Have

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
4+ years of professional software development experience or a similar role
Strong knowledge of full-stack engineering principles and system design.
Experience with programming languages such as Python, Javascript, React, and SQL.
Experience building 0-1 products
Demonstrated strong problem-solving skills and effective communication abilities.
Eagerness to collaborate and ability to engage confidently with clients.
Adaptability and enthusiasm for working in a fast-paced, client-focused healthcare environment.

new_jobs.title: Founding Solutions Engineer, Data & AI Infrastructure
new_jobs.description:
Build the foundation for what’s next in financial technology.

Financial data is everywhere. Making it accessible, reliable, and useful remains one of the hardest challenges in financial technology. WealthArc is changing that.
We’re building independent global financial data infrastructure that connects financial institutions, standardizes complex financial data, and makes it usable by AI agents, intelligent systems, applications, developers, and businesses that depend on it. Through modern APIs, unified financial data models, and emerging interfaces such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), we help AI agent developers and financial institutions build what comes next.
We’re looking for a Founding Solutions Engineer
to help bring that vision to life.

The opportunity

This isn’t a traditional presales role. You’ll be an early member of WealthArc’s go-to-market team, working closely with our Chief Growth Officer, product leaders, and engineers to help customers understand, evaluate, and build on our platform.
A key part of the role will be introducing WealthArc to AI companies developing agents and applications for wealth and asset management - and showing them how trusted, standardized financial data can help their products work across institutions and markets. You’ll build relationships across the AI agents ecosystem and help WealthArc become a partner of choice for companies bringing AI into financial services.
One day you might help a developer integrate using our APIs. The next, you could work with a global wealth manager on its data architecture or show an AI company how trusted financial data can power intelligent applications. You’ll shape both how we win customers and how they experience WealthArc.

What you'll do

Make complex technology easy to understand 

Lead technical discovery to understand a customer’s architecture, data challenges, use cases, and goals.
Turn technical capabilities into clear demonstrations, solution designs, and business outcomes.
Build credibility with developers and data engineers as well as CTOs, CIOs, and executive leadership.

Help developers build on WealthArc 

Develop deep expertise in our global data infrastructure, APIs, standardized financial objects, and MCP capabilities.
Work hands-on with AI agent developers and financial institutions’ data and technical teams to validate use cases, answer integration questions, and troubleshoot issues.
Lead API evaluations, proof-of-concept projects, and pilots, including data testing and validation.
Improve our developer experience through examples, sandbox workflows, documentation, and reference architectures.
Collaborate across internal teams to enhance the WealthArc Developer Hub, creating resources such as GitHub repositories, code snippets, use case examples, and live or recorded demos that streamline integration and showcase our data infrastructure.

Build relationships across the AI agents ecosystem

Identify and engage AI companies developing agents and applications for wealth and asset management.
Build a strong network among AI companies, agent developers, and relevant ecosystem partners.
Understand the AI agents landscape, including emerging companies, products, use cases, and the relationships shaping the ecosystem.
Explain how WealthArc’s data infrastructure can help AI companies develop, evaluate, and scale their products across financial institutions and markets.
Gather ecosystem feedback and share insights on partnership opportunities, customer needs, and market developments with the growth, product, and engineering teams.

Own the technical side of the sales process 

Partner with growth and business development from discovery through technical validation and commercial close.
Support sales conversations with AI companies and other technology providers, connecting their product requirements to WealthArc’s capabilities.
Design tailored demonstrations and help customers understand how WealthArc fits within their existing systems.
Surface technical requirements and risks early; contribute to proposals, solution architectures, and enterprise evaluations.

Help shape what comes next 

Bring customer and ecosystem feedback directly to product and engineering to help prioritize improvements.
Create reusable technical assets that make evaluations faster and the team more effective.
Help define and scale the solutions engineering function as WealthArc grows.

What we're looking for

5–7 years of relevant experience in financial data engineering, solutions engineering, sales engineering, API or MCP development, or technical consulting.
Strong technical knowledge of APIs, MCP, enterprise data integration, cloud data architecture, and data-sharing architectures.
Hands-on experience with tools such as Postman, SQL, Python, or similar technologies to support technical discovery and integration.
Experience supporting or leading enterprise sales engagements, including technical discovery, qualification, solution design, demonstrations, and proofs of concept.
Ability to understand customer technology environments and translate technical capabilities into business value.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to engage C-level executives, enterprise architects, developers, and business stakeholders.
A strong consultative approach, with the ability to influence technical decisions, build customer confidence, and support commercial outcomes.
Interest in building relationships and developing a network across AI companies and the AI agents ecosystem.

Experience that would stand out

Wealth management, WealthTech, FinTech, banking, custody, or financial data infrastructure experience.
Experience at a modern enterprise data or API-first company, such as Snowflake, Databricks, or a comparable platform.
Familiarity with public and private markets data, including client accounts, holdings, transactions, securities, and reference data across custodians and banks, as well as data normalization and reconciliation.
Experience working with AI companies, AI agent developers, or companies building AI-focused applications and infrastructure.
An established network across AI companies, developers, or the AI agents ecosystem.
Exposure to and/or experience building LLMs, AI agents, or AI-focused developer infrastructure.

*You don’t need to check every box. We value technical curiosity, sound judgment, customer empathy, and the ability to learn quickly. 

Why WealthArc

Work on foundational infrastructure.
Trusted financial data is essential to the next generation of financial applications and AI.
Make an outsized impact.
As an early go-to-market hire, you’ll influence customers, product priorities, and how we scale.
Build with a global team.
Collaborate across the U.S., Europe, and Asia on challenges spanning markets, technologies, and borders.
Own the developer experience.
Help make sophisticated infrastructure intuitive to evaluate, integrate, and use.

Come build it with us 

AI agents, AI applications, and the next generation of financial products will depend on trusted, accessible, actionable data. We’re building the infrastructure that makes it possible.

new_jobs.title: Solutions Engineer, AI Build Team
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The AI Build team is a new, industry-focused team dedicated to building with the world’s leading and fastest-scaling AI companies. We work alongside Stripe’s AI Solutions Architecture and GTM teams, and across Stripe’s product suite to help customers adopt emerging products, close interoperability and 0→1 solution gaps, and bring field learning directly into Stripe’s product roadmap. The team owns strategic proof-of-concept engagements across the pre- and post-sales lifecycle, complementing Stripe’s AI account teams and the product depth of Stripe’s specialist teams.

What you'll do

As a Solutions Engineer on the AI Build team, you’ll work directly with frontier AI companies on the payments, billing, and monetization infrastructure underlying their core businesses. You’ll own complex proof-of-concept engagements on Stripe’s frontier products, from initial scoping through activation and handoff, combining customer discovery, solution design, rapid prototyping, and cross-functional leadership. You won’t simply implement a finished product: you’ll build with customers, identify where Stripe’s products or integrations need to evolve, and help customers feel as though they are inside our product roadmap.

Responsibilities

Own strategic POCs end to end: Sell, scope, and lead proof-of-concept engagements from initial customer commitment through activation.
Build with customers: Work deeply with users’ engineers and technical leaders to understand their workflows, rapidly prototype solutions, and establish credible paths to production.
Design across Stripe: Create solutions that span multiple Stripe products and determine whether blockers require configuration, integration work, custom development, or a core product change.
Close 0→1 gaps: Navigate incomplete products, evolving requirements, and interoperability gaps while balancing immediate customer outcomes with reusable solutions.
Influence the roadmap: Translate customer needs and deployment friction into clear product requirements, and partner with product and engineering teams to shape how Stripe’s frontier products are built.
Lead cross-functionally: Coordinate AI account teams, AI and specialist Solutions Architects, product and engineering teams, Professional Services, and post-sales technical resources across the engagement lifecycle of new builds and deployments.
Create repeatable patterns: Turn successful customer-specific work into reusable prototypes, reference architectures, implementation playbooks, and solution components.
Stay close to the AI frontier: Operate at the pace and in the working style of AI-native companies, and remain current on emerging companies, products, business models, and technical developments across the industry.

Who you are

You are a customer-oriented technical builder who thrives in ambiguous, fast-moving environments. You build trusted relationships with engineers, technical leaders, and senior stakeholders, and you are equally comfortable discovering an unclear problem, designing an architecture, prototyping a solution, and coordinating teams through activation. You use code pragmatically to accelerate your work. You communicate clearly, lead through influence, and look for patterns that can turn one customer engagement into a better product or repeatable approach for many customers.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of relevant experience in customer-facing technical delivery, solutions engineering, implementation, technical product management, or a related field
Experience owning complex customer engagements from discovery and solution design through implementation or activation, including work across both pre- and post-sales phases
Demonstrated success in ambiguous, 0→1 environments where the standard product, integration, or implementation pattern did not yet exist
Strong understanding of APIs, integrations, application architecture, and data flows, with the judgment to distinguish implementation gaps from core product gaps
Ability to prototype rapidly using modern AI coding harnesses and development tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex
Working proficiency in one or more relevant languages, such as Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Ruby; depth in a particular language is less important than the ability to learn quickly and build credible prototypes
Ability to build trusted relationships with customer engineers, technical leaders, founders, and other senior stakeholders
Ability to lead through influence across sales, product, engineering, implementation, and post-sales teams while maintaining clear ownership of the customer outcome
Experience operating at startup speed and in Slack-first, rapidly changing environments, along with active engagement in the broader AI industry

This role offers a unique opportunity to partner directly with leading AI companies and work on the financial infrastructure that powers their businesses. As an early member of Stripe’s AI industry team, you’ll help shape how Stripe partners with frontier companies, brings emerging products to market, and translates customer insights into product direction.

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $239,900 - $359,900. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

new_jobs.title: Sr Software Engineer I, Forward Deployed Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.
Your Impact

Dedrone by Axon protects airspace from drone threats. Each deployment combines our software, our own and partner sensors, and a networking stack that connects the site to DedroneC2 in the cloud. As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you are part of the team that owns the technical outcome at our most critical customer sites. This is a software and systems role. You work mostly through remote access to customer sites, and our installation teams and partners do the physical work.
You take each problem from live triage to a fix in the field, then make sure the long-term fix lands in the product. You have the authority to raise defects and to join design reviews with our product teams, based on what you see first-hand. One question guides the work: how do we leave the product better than we found it, so nobody has to work this issue again?
What You’ll Do

Location: Hybrid. Up to 20% travel required, to customer sites, demonstrations, and exercises.
Must be within commutable distance to one of our Hub locations listed below: Sterling VA)
Reports to: Engineering Manager, Forward Deployed Engineering
Own complex site issues end to end: lead the incident, get the site working, and write the review afterwards.
Resolve live site problems that Support escalates, diagnosing failures across software, sensors, and networks with customers and installers.
Write the fixes, integrations, and automation that get a site working, and set the quality bar for field fixes through code reviews.
Leave no one-off behind: move each site-specific fix into the product or retire it, and follow the root cause with our product teams until the fix ships.
Set the standards for the runbooks, checklists, acceptance tests, and monitoring that make deployments repeatable.
Mentor engineers on the team, and coach Support and installers on what you learn.
Take part in the engineering on-call rota.
Use AI-assisted engineering tools across your work, and help the team use them well.

What You Bring

6+ years of experience in software engineering, site reliability, or systems integration
Production ownership: you have been on call, led incidents, and debugged live systems from logs and metrics
Proficiency in at least one programming language, such as Python or Java, with a record of shipping code to production
Clear communication with customers, installers, and engineers during live incidents
Experience mentoring engineers and conducting technical interviews
Hands-on experience with AI-assisted engineering tools and workflows
Deep experience in one of these: Software: you have designed and owned production services, and you can find and fix a defect in a large codebase that you did not write.
Systems: you have deployed and troubleshot Linux systems and IP networks at production or customer sites, including integration with third-party equipment.

Work Location

This role is based out of our Sterling Office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.
Benefits that Benefit You
Competitive salary and 401k with employer match
Discretionary paid time off
Paid parental leave for all
Medical, Dental, Vision plans
Fitness Programs
Emotional & Mental Wellness support
Learning & Development programs
Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)
And yes, we have snacks in our offices

Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.

Axon is a total compensation company, meaning compensation is made up of base pay, bonus, and stock awards. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: level, function, training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs, geographic market, and often a combination of all these factors. Our benefits offer an array of options to help support you physically, financially and emotionally through the big milestones and in your everyday life. To see more details on our benefits offerings please visit https://www.axon.com/careers.
Base Pay Range: $141,000 USD - $225,600 USD
Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.
Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.
Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.
We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at  axongreenhousesupport@axon.com
 or via our Axon Privacy Web Form. For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.
Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment.
We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes.
Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers.  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com
, or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, US
new_jobs.description:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About The Role

UFORCE is hiring a US Forward Deployed Engineer to deploy forward with customers and internal teams to make UFORCE systems work reliably in real-world environments. This role is focused on UAS and/or USV systems across exercises, red-team events, demos, and customer operations.

You will own end-to-end field integration, troubleshooting, and customer success across one or more technical disciplines — systems, networking, hardware, autonomy, software, electronics, or payload integration — and turn field learnings into repeatable kits, test plans, playbooks, and engineering improvements.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who can operate calmly under pressure, translate between operators and engineers, and make mission-ready capability the standard.

What you’ll do

Deploy forward to customer sites, ranges, exercises, and operational environments to prepare, integrate, test, troubleshoot, and sustain UFORCE systems.
Lead technical readiness for major exercises, red-team events, and customer contracts, including pre-ship, arrival, pre-mission, and go/no-go gates.
Own field incident response: diagnose issues, create minimal reproductions, capture evidence, coordinate fixes, and drive root-cause closure.
Build deployment evidence packages, including configuration baselines, network diagrams, spectrum/safety approvals, software versions, test results, and logs.
Create and maintain standardized deployment kits, spares packages, images, configs, scripts, and field playbooks.
Partner with engineering teams to convert field failures and operator feedback into validated software, autonomy, hardware, network, payload, and process improvements.
Maintain customer and internal operating cadence through crisp status updates, risk tracking, decision logs, AARs, and action-item closeout.
Help train operators, maintainers, and internal teams so deployments become more repeatable over time.

What success looks like

Supported major exercises and customer operations with strong technical readiness, high mission availability, and no mission-stopping technical aborts attributable to integration or setup.
Reduced recurring field issues and MTTR through disciplined troubleshooting, evidence capture, and root-cause resolution.
Established complete, repeatable deployment evidence kits and AAR processes that help the team move faster without sacrificing safety, compliance, or configuration control.
Built deployment kits and playbooks that reduce setup-to-ready time and make sustainment easier in austere environments.
Delivered field-driven engineering improvements that are validated on range and reflected in released builds or configurations.

What we’re looking for

Deep hands-on experience in at least one relevant technical specialty: systems engineering, network engineering, autonomy, software, electronics, payload integration, or hardware.
Experience working with UAS and/or USV systems, or closely related deployed robotics, autonomy, defense, maritime, aerospace, or field-engineered systems.
Strong field integration instincts: configuration baselines, build-to-deploy workflows, imaging, version control, automated checks, and release discipline.
Practical networking knowledge, including IP planning, routing/switching, RF/spectrum constraints, secure comms basics, logging, and telemetry.
Strong troubleshooting toolkit: logs, packet captures, electrical debugging, scripting, automated checks, and disciplined test planning.
Ability to operate in environments requiring access control, least privilege, auditability, and sound security posture.
Clear communication with customers, operators, engineers, PMs, and executives — especially under time pressure.
High ownership, strong judgment, and a bias toward evidence-based execution over hero debugging.

Required

US citizen.
TS/SCI cleared or credibly eligible.
Willing to deploy forward for exercises, red-team events, demos, and customer operations.
Comfortable working hands-on in austere environments such as shipboard, range, remote, or irregular-hours settings.

Nice to have

Prior FDE, FSR, field engineering, or deployment experience supporting defense programs, exercises, SOCOM, Navy, Army, or similar users.
Experience with autonomy tuning, GNSS-denied environments, EW/spectrum coordination, safety-of-flight, or safety approvals.
Experience building evidence or compliance kits, including configuration management, test artifacts, and ATO-style workflows.
Instructor mindset and experience training customers, operators, maintainers, or internal teams.

How we work

We optimize for mission readiness, evidence-based execution, tempo with safety, and customer trust. The right person for this role is a systems thinker and hands-on doer who can move from symptoms to hypotheses to tests to fixes — while keeping operators, customers, and engineering teams aligned.

The nature of combat has changed.

Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability.

And UFORCE is ready.

Are You?

.

and architectural integrity. Rather than letting individual squads build bespoke cloud setups, fragile CI/CD pipelines, or one-off integration forks from scratch, you abstract every field solution into reusable, self-service "golden paths"
—so the entire engineering organization ships faster, safer, and with dramatically lower cognitive load.

Abstract squad-specific infrastructure and integration needs into reusable self-service templates, SDKs, and paved platform roads (e.g., Backstage, Crossplane, GitOps)—eliminating bespoke core forks and duplicated engineering effort.

Design airtight data synchronization, schema transformation, reconciliation, idempotency, retry, and dead-letter queue (DLQ) mechanisms.

Instrument all paved-road middleware and platform services with standardized centralized logging, metrics, and distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, ELK) to guarantee aggressive enterprise SLAs.

.

Externally, you will author blog posts, reference architectures, and perspective documents that establish AWS's point of view in the ADAS, autonomous vehicle, and physical AI domains.

Internally, you will drive field enablement — creating artifacts, tools, and training content that empower the broader SA community to position and deliver autonomous operations solutions. new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

About The Role

We’re looking for exceptional engineers to help build the ML Platform that powers our tabular foundation model line. This is a unique chance to work at the intersection of data science, agents, UX, and real-world economic impact.

You'll work on the product end-to-end: frontend, backend, and everything in between.

What you'll work on:

Build the core platform that puts tabular foundation models into users' hands — from data upload and exploration through inference and results
Architect reliable, low-latency backend services that handle real-time model inference at scale
Work directly with the research team to turn new model capabilities into production features
Own the frontend experience for technical users (data scientists, ML engineers) who have high expectations and low tolerance for friction

You may be a good fit if you have:

3+ years building highly-available, user-facing products across the full stack, with real ownership of what shipped
Experience building data-intensive applications (dashboards, analytics tools, data exploration interfaces, or similar)
Strong JavaScript/TypeScript and Python — you're genuinely good at both, not just passable in one
Experience with React, FastAPI, and Postgres (our current stack)
Good product instincts — you think about what the user actually needs, not just what the ticket says
Comfort working close to ML systems, even if you're not training models yourself — you understand model inputs, outputs, and failure modes well enough to build reliable interfaces around them
Enthusiasm for working in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where new ideas ship quickly and user impact matters most

Bonus:

Cloud infrastructure experience (GCP preferred)
Background building developer tools, data platforms, or ML-adjacent products

Life at Prior Labs

You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.

Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.

Our Commitments

The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.

Company Overview

Balchem is committed to making the world a healthier place by delivering trusted, innovative, and science-based solutions for the health and nutritional needs of the world. Balchem employs approximately 1,400 employees worldwide who provide the service, quality, and technology that enables our customers to win with their customers. We have built a reputation for delivering results to all of our stakeholders. Founded in 1967, Balchem, a Maryland corporation, became a publicly-traded company in 1970 and is listed on Nasdaq under the symbol “BCPC.” Our corporate headquarters is located in Montvale, New Jersey, and we have a broad network of sales offices, manufacturing sites, and R&D centers, primarily located in the U.S. and Europe. The Company consists of three business segments: Human Nutrition and Health, Animal Nutrition and Health, and Specialty Products.

Position Summary

The AI Engineer will design, build, and deploy AI agents and AI-enabled automations for Balchem's supporting functions (Finance, Operations, HR, Legal, etc.) and Business Segments. This is a hands-on technical role focused on applying commercially available AI platforms and large language models to real business processes, not on building or training foundation models.

Success in this role requires strong software development and integration skills, practical experience with generative AI and agent tooling, and the business acumen to turn a process problem into a working, reliable solution. The AI Engineer will collaborate with functional teams to understand how work gets done today, then build agents that connect to Balchem's systems and data and deliver measurable productivity gains.

While working closely with specific business segments and functions to ensure each solution fits its context, the AI Engineer builds with an enterprise-wide perspective, favoring reusable components, common standards, and secure, supportable designs that can scale across Balchem.

The AI Engineer will work within Balchem's AI Governance Process, helping to execute the Corporate AI Strategy by delivering prioritized use cases and ensuring every solution meets the organization's AI guardrails for security, privacy, and responsible use.

Essential Functions

AI Agent Design & Development

Design, build, and deploy AI agents, copilots, and assistants using existing AI platforms, large language models, and agent frameworks to automate and improve business processes across Balchem's functions and business segments.

Systems Integration & Automation

Integrate AI agents with Balchem's enterprise applications and data sources (ERP, CRM, collaboration, and data platforms) using APIs, connectors, and workflow tools.
Build AI-driven automations that reduce manual steps, shorten cycle times, and improve the accuracy of routine work.

Solution Delivery & Lifecycle Management

Own the full delivery lifecycle for AI solutions, from requirements and prototyping through testing, deployment, documentation, and ongoing support.
Translate business requirements into technical designs and help prioritize the delivery backlog based on potential benefit and business objectives.
Ensure solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and with measurable business impact.

Use Case Discovery & Prototyping

Work with business stakeholders to identify and assess high-value use cases for AI agents and automation across the organization.
Build rapid prototypes and proofs of concept to validate feasibility and value before committing to full development.

Prompt Engineering & Knowledge Grounding

Apply prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and tool calling to ground agents in Balchem's data and knowledge, improving the accuracy, relevance, and reliability of their output.

User Enablement & Adoption

Support the rollout of new AI solutions with clear documentation, demonstrations, and hands-on guidance for end users.
Partner with functional teams to gather feedback, resolve issues, and refine solutions so they are adopted and continue to deliver value.

Security, Compliance & Responsible AI

Build solutions that protect company data by applying appropriate access controls, data handling practices, and testing for accuracy and misuse.
Ensure all solutions comply with Balchem's AI Policy and IT security standards.

Monitoring & Continuous Improvement

Monitor the usage, quality, and cost of deployed agents, track KPIs, and continuously tune solutions to improve their performance and impact.

Collaboration & Technology Awareness

Work closely with IT, cybersecurity, and business teams, and stay current on emerging AI tools and practices to recommend those that fit Balchem's needs.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of experience in software development, automation, or systems integration, including at least a year of hands-on work building generative AI solutions.
Demonstrated experience building and deploying AI agents or LLM-powered applications into production using existing platforms and APIs (for example, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI services, or comparable agent frameworks).
Working knowledge of large language models, prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, agent orchestration, and solution evaluation. Experience training or building foundation models is not required.
Proficiency in Python or a similar language, REST APIs, and low-code automation tools, with experience integrating solutions into enterprise systems such as ERP, CRM, and Microsoft 365.
Understanding of data security, privacy, and responsible AI practices, with a commitment to continuous learning as AI technologies and best practices evolve.
Strong communication, collaboration skills and documentation skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and work effectively with business stakeholders.
